entries.question: How many records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_record as (
  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CIVIL_RIGHTS.CIVIL_RIGHTS__FED_NARA_WRA_AAD
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many complaints appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits complaints into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means complaint ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_complaint as (
  select COMPLAINT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CONSUMER_PROTECTION.CONSUMER_PROTECTION__FED_CFPB_COMPLAINTS
  where COMPLAINT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_complaint;

entries.means: Splits recall records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_recall_record as (
  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CONSUMER_SAFETY.CONSUMER_SAFETY__FED_NHTSA_RECALLS
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_recall_record;

  select NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORPORATE_REGISTRY.CORPORATE_REGISTRY__FED_ICIJ_OFFSHORELEAKS_ADDRESSES
  where NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_name;

entries.question: How many nodes appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits nodes into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means node ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_node as (
  select NODE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORPORATE_REGISTRY.CORPORATE_REGISTRY__FED_ICIJ_OFFSHORELEAKS_INTERMEDIARIES
  where NODE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_node;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORPORATE_REGISTRY.CORPORATE_REGISTRY__FED_IRS_EO_BMF
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.question: How many corporate registries appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits corporate registries into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means corporate registry key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_corporate_registry as (
  select CORPORATE_REGISTRY_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORPORATE_REGISTRY.CORPORATE_REGISTRY__INTL_IE_CRO
  where CORPORATE_REGISTRY_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_corporate_registry;

entries.question: How many companies appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits companies into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means company number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_company as (
  select COMPANY_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.CORPORATE_REGISTRY.CORPORATE_REGISTRY__UK_COMPANIES_HOUSE_PSC
  where COMPANY_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_company;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_DOL_FORM5500
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT
  where REPORT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_FOREIGNASSISTANCE
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many opportunities appear more than once (going by opportunity ID)?
entries.means: Splits opportunities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means opportunity ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_opportunity as (
  select OPPORTUNITY_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_GRANTS_GOV
  where OPPORTUNITY_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_opportunity;

entries.question: How many returns appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits returns into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means return ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_return as (
  select RETURN_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_990_EFILE_INDEX
  where RETURN_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_return;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_BMF
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_EO_PR
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organisations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organisations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means EIN is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organisation as (
  select EIN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_REVOCATION
  where EIN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organisation;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many borrowers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits borrowers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means borrower name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_borrower as (
  select BORROWER_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_SBA_LOANS
  where BORROWER_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_borrower;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many lines appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits lines into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means src line nbr is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_line as (
  select SRC_LINE_NBR, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_DEBT_OUTSTANDING
  where SRC_LINE_NBR is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_line;

  select PARENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_TREASURY_MTS_RECEIPTS
  where PARENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_parent;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many assistance transactions appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits assistance transactions into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means assistance transaction unique key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_assistance_transaction as (
  select ASSISTANCE_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_ASSISTANCE_FULL
  where ASSISTANCE_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_assistance_transaction;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contract awards appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contract awards into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contract award unique key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contract_award as (
  select CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS
  where CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contract_award;

from first_seen
group by 1

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contract transactions appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contract transactions into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contract transaction unique key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contract_transaction as (
  select CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS_FULL
  where CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contract_transaction;

entries.question: How many awards appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits awards into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means award ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_award as (
  select AWARD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__FED_US_USASPENDING_API
  where AWARD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_award;

entries.question: How many advertisers appear more than once?

entries.sql:
with per_advertiser as (
  select ADVERTISER_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.EDUCATION.EDUCATION__FED_GOOGLE_POLADS_ADVERTISER_DECLARED_STATS
  where ADVERTISER_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_advertiser;

entries.means: Splits advertisers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means advertiser ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_advertiser as (
  select ADVERTISER_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.EDUCATION.EDUCATION__FED_GOOGLE_POLADS_ADVERTISER_STATS
  where ADVERTISER_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_advertiser;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many filings appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits filings into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means filing uuid is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_filing as (
  select FILING_UUID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.EDUCATION.EDUCATION__FED_SENATE_LDA_FILINGS
  where FILING_UUID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_filing;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many utilities appear more than once (going by utility ID)?
entries.means: Splits utilities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means utility ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_utility as (
  select UTILITY_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA860_1_UTILITY
  where UTILITY_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_utility;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_ownership;

entries.sql:
with per_generator as (
  select GENERATOR_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA860_3_3_SOLAR
  where GENERATOR_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_generator;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many generators appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits generators into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means generator ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_generator as (
  select GENERATOR_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA860_3_4_ENERGY_STORAGE
  where GENERATOR_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_generator;

entries.means: Splits generators into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means generator ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.

  select GENERATOR_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA860_3_5_MULTIFUEL
  where GENERATOR_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_generator;

entries.question: How many generators appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits generators into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means generator ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_generator as (
  select GENERATOR_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA860_4_OWNER
  where GENERATOR_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_generator;

)

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA861_OPERATIONAL_DATA

  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_record;

entries.question: How many records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_record as (
  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA861_SALES_ULT_CUST
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_record;

entries.question: How many utility per states appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits utility per states into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_utility_per_state as (
  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENERGY.ENERGY__FED_EIA861_UTILITY_DATA
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_utility_per_state;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many aqs sites appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits aqs sites into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means aqs site ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_aqs_site as (
  select AQS_SITE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_AQS_SITES
  where AQS_SITE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_aqs_site;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many facilities appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits facilities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means facility name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_facility as (
  select FACILITY_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_ECHO
  where FACILITY_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_facility;

entries.sql:

  select HANDLER_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_ENVIROFACTS
  where HANDLER_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_GHGRP_FACILITY
  where FACILITY_YEAR_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_facility_year;

entries.means: Splits npdes into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means npdes ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_npdes as (
  select NPDES_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_NPDES_ICIS_FACILITIES
  where NPDES_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_npdes;

entries.means: Splits enforcement records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means enforcement record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_enforcement_record as (
  select ENFORCEMENT_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_RCRA_ENFORCEMENTS
  where ENFORCEMENT_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_enforcement_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_FACILITIES
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_GEOGRAPHIC_AREAS
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_SITE_VISITS
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_VIOLATIONS_ENFORCEMENT
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many boundary features appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits boundary features into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means boundary feature ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_boundary_feature as (
  select BOUNDARY_FEATURE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_SUPERFUND_SITE_BOUNDARIES
  where BOUNDARY_FEATURE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_boundary_feature;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many c 3 frs appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits c 3 frs into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means c 3 frs ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_c_3_frs as (
  select C_3_FRS_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_EPA_TRI_BASIC_2023
  where C_3_FRS_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_c_3_frs;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many other structures appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits other structures into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means other structure ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_other_structure as (
  select OTHER_STRUCTURE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_NID_DAMS
  where OTHER_STRUCTURE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_other_structure;

entries.question: How many episodes appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits episodes into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means episode ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_episode as (
  select EPISODE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_STORM_EVENTS
  where EPISODE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_episode;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_PHMSA_FLAGGED_INCIDENTS
  where REPORT_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.question: How many well records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits well records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means well record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_well_record as (
  select WELL_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_ORPHANED_OIL_GAS_WELLS
  where WELL_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_well_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many globals appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits globals into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means global ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_global as (
  select GLOBAL_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_USGS_WBD_HUC8
  where GLOBAL_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_global;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many organization identifiers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits organization identifiers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means organization identifier is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_organization_identifier as (
  select ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_WQP_MONITORING_STATIONS
  where ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_organization_identifier;

entries.question: How many defenders appear more than once?

entries.sql:
with per_defender as (
  select DEFENDER_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__INTL_GLOBAL_WITNESS_DEFENDERS
  where DEFENDER_NAME is not null

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_defender;

entries.question: How many activities appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits activities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means activity ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_activity as (
  select ACTIVITY_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_EPA_ICIS_FEC_CASE_ENFORCEMENT_CONCLUSION_FACILITIES
  where ACTIVITY_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_activity;

entries.question: How many registered sites appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits registered sites into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means registry ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_registered_site as (
  select REGISTRY_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_EPA_ICIS_FEC_ICIS_FEC_EPA_INSPECTIONS
  where REGISTRY_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_registered_site;

entries.question: How many branch years appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits branch years into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means branch year key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_branch_year as (
  select BRANCH_YEAR_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_FDIC_SOD_BRANCH_DEPOSITS
  where BRANCH_YEAR_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_branch_year;

entries.question: How many political committees appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits political committees into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means cmte ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_political_committee as (
  select CMTE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_FEC_CAND_CMTE_LINKAGE
  where CMTE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_political_committee;

entries.means: Splits files into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means file num is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_file as (
  select FILE_NUM, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_FEC_COMMITTEE_TO_CANDIDATE
  where FILE_NUM is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_file;

)

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_political_committee;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many fhfas appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits fhfas into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means fhfa ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_fhfa as (
  select FHFA_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_FHFA_FHLB_MEMBERSHIP
  where FHFA_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_fhfa;

entries.means: Splits datasets into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means dataset name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_dataset as (
  select DATASET_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_IRS_SOI
  where DATASET_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_dataset;

  where JOIN_NUMBER is not null

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_join;

entries.question: How many form filings appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits form filings into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means form filing ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_form_filing as (
  select FORM_FILING_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_PCAOB_FORM_AP_FILINGS
  where FORM_FILING_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_form_filing;

entries.question: How many filings appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits filings into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means accession number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_filing as (
  select ACCESSION_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_SEC_13F_HOLDINGS
  where ACCESSION_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_filing;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many companies appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits companies into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means CIK is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_company as (
  select CIK, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_SEC_EDGAR_FINANCIALS
  where CIK is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_company;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many filings appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits filings into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means accession number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_filing as (
  select ACCESSION_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_SEC_INSIDER_DERIV_TRANS
  where ACCESSION_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_filing;

  select ACCESSION_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_SEC_INSIDER_REPORTINGOWNER
  where ACCESSION_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_filing;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many series class records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits series class records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means series class record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_series_class_record as (
  select SERIES_CLASS_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FINANCE.FINANCE__FED_SEC_INVESTMENT_COMPANY_SERIES_CLASS
  where SERIES_CLASS_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_series_class_record;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_series;

entries.question: How many fara registrations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits fara registrations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means fara registration key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_fara_registration as (
  select FARA_REGISTRATION_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.FOREIGN_INFLUENCE.FOREIGN_INFLUENCE__FED_FARA_BULK
  where FARA_REGISTRATION_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_fara_registration;

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.GOVERNMENT_RECORDS.GOVERNMENT_RECORDS__FED_NARA_AAD
  where PERSON_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_person;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many units appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits units into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means unit num is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_unit as (
  select UNIT_NUM, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CDC_SUICIDE_RATES
  where UNIT_NUM is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_unit;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many certified facilities appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits certified facilities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ccn is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_certified_facility as (
  select CCN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_DIALYSIS
  where CCN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_certified_facility;

entries.question: How many enrollments appear more than once?

  select ENROLLMENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_FEDERALLY_QUALIFIED_HEALTH_CENTER_ENROLLMENTS
  where ENROLLMENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_enrollment;

entries.question: How many medicare CBSAs appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits medicare CBSAs into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means medicare CBSA number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_medicare_cbsa as (
  select MEDICARE_CBSA_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_HCRIS
  where MEDICARE_CBSA_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_medicare_cbsa;
entries.dataset: The detailed financial accounts hospitals file with Medicare.

entries.means: Splits providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means provider name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_provider as (
  select PROVIDER_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_HOME_HEALTH
  where PROVIDER_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_provider;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_certified_facility;

entries.question: How many certified facilities appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits certified facilities into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ccn is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_certified_facility as (
  select CCN, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_GENERAL
  where CCN is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_certified_facility;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many healthcare providers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits healthcare providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means NPI is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_healthcare_provider as (
  select NPI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_HPT_MRF
  where NPI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_healthcare_provider;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

entries.means: Splits healthcare providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means NPI is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_healthcare_provider as (
  select NPI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DIALYSIS_FACILITIES
  where NPI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_healthcare_provider;

entries.sql:
select a.CCN,
       count(*) as n_facilities
from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DIALYSIS_FACILITIES as a
join LIBRARY_MARTS.FINDINGS.HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK as b
  on a.CCN = b.CCN
where a.CCN is not null
group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 100;

entries.question: How many rbcs appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits rbcs into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means rbcs ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_rbcs as (
  select RBCS_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_MEDICARE_DURABLE_MEDICAL_EQUIPMENT_DEVICES_SUPPLIES_BY_SUPPL
  where RBCS_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_rbcs;

entries.means: Splits healthcare providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means NPI is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_healthcare_provider as (
  select NPI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS
  where NPI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_healthcare_provider;

entries.question: How many payment records per healthcare provider, matched against another dataset?
entries.means: NPI also appears in 34 other tables - the same healthcare provider can be matched across both. Check both sides use the identifier the same way; padding and blanks have faked matches before.
entries.sql:
select a.NPI,
       count(*) as n_payment_records
from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS as a
join LIBRARY_MARTS.FINDINGS.EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_AT_FACILITY as b
  on a.NPI = b.NPI
where a.NPI is not null
group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 100;

entries.question: How many payment records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits payment records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:

  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS_2023
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_payment_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many cross ref providers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits cross ref providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means cross ref provider number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_cross_ref_provider as (
  select CROSS_REF_PROVIDER_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_POS_OTHER
  where CROSS_REF_PROVIDER_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_cross_ref_provider;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many providers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means provider key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_provider as (
  select PROVIDER_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_QUALITY_PAYMENT_PROGRAM_EXPERIENCE
  where PROVIDER_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_provider;

group by 1
order by 2 desc

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many enrollments appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits enrollments into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means enrollment ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_enrollment as (
  select ENROLLMENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_RURAL_HEALTH_CLINIC_ENROLLMENTS
  where ENROLLMENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_enrollment;

entries.means: Splits enrollments into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means enrollment ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_enrollment as (
  select ENROLLMENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_CMS_SKILLED_NURSING_FACILITY_ENROLLMENTS
  where ENROLLMENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_enrollment;

       count(*) as n_enrolments

  on a.NPI = b.NPI
where a.NPI is not null
group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 100;

  where ripple_ts is not null and TRANSACTION_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select yr, count(*) as n_new
from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.sql:
with per_recall as (
  select RECALL_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_FDA_DEVICE_ENFORCEMENT
  where RECALL_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_recall;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many recalls appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits recalls into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means recall number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_recall as (
  select RECALL_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_FDA_DRUG_ENFORCEMENT
  where RECALL_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_recall;

  select REGISTRATION_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_FDA_ESTABLISHMENT_REG
  where REGISTRATION_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_registration;

entries.question: How many public device records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public device records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means public device record key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_device_record as (
  select PUBLIC_DEVICE_RECORD_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_FDA_GUDID
  where PUBLIC_DEVICE_RECORD_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_device_record;

entries.question: How many mdr reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits mdr reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means mdr report key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_mdr_report as (
  select MDR_REPORT_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_FDA_MAUDE
  where MDR_REPORT_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_mdr_report;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many healthcare providers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits healthcare providers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means NPI is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_healthcare_provider as (
  select NPI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE
  where NPI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_healthcare_provider;

entries.question: How many hpsa components appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits hpsa components into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means hpsa component ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_hpsa_component as (
  select HPSA_COMPONENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_HRSA_HPSA_PRIMARY_CARE
  where HPSA_COMPONENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_hpsa_component;

entries.question: How many payments show up for the first time each year?

entries.sql:
with first_seen as (
  select PAYMENT_NUMBER, min(year(ripple_ts)) as yr
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TIMELINE.HEALTH__FED_HRSA_NPDB
  where ripple_ts is not null and PAYMENT_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select yr, count(*) as n_new
from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many hpsas appear more than once (going by hpsa ID)?
entries.means: Splits hpsas into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means hpsa ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_hpsa as (
  select HPSA_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HEALTH.HEALTH__FED_HRSA_SHORTAGE_AREAS
  where HPSA_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_hpsa;

entries.question: How many federally-funded health centers per year?
entries.means: The trend by year. The date means when it was reported, which can be long after. Counts records, not events - a rise can mean more happening or more being logged.

entries.question: How many owneras appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits owneras into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ownera is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_ownera as (
  select OWNERA, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HISTORY.HISTORY__FED_SLAVEVOYAGES_TRANSATLANTIC
  where OWNERA is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_ownera;

entries.question: How many co applicant credit score types appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits co applicant credit score types into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means co applicant credit score type is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_co_applicant_credit_score_type as (
  select CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_DC_ONLY
  where CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_co_applicant_credit_score_type;

entries.question: How many mortgage application records per legal entity, matched against another dataset?
entries.means: LEI also appears in 6 other tables - the same legal entity can be matched across both. Check both sides use the identifier the same way; padding and blanks have faked matches before.
entries.sql:
select a.LEI,
       count(*) as n_mortgage_application_records
from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_DC_ONLY as a
join LIBRARY_MARTS.ECONOMICS.ECONOMICS__INTL_GLEIF as b
  on a.LEI = b.LEI
where a.LEI is not null
group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 100;

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TIMELINE.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_HISTORIC
  where ripple_ts is not null and RESPONDENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)

from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many respondents appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits respondents into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means respondent ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_respondent as (
  select RESPONDENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_HISTORIC
  where RESPONDENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_respondent;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many lar records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits lar records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means lar record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_lar_record as (
  select LAR_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_CFPB_HMDA_LAR
  where LAR_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_lar_record;

entries.question: How many loan-level mortgage application records per legal entity, matched against another dataset?
entries.means: LEI also appears in 6 other tables - the same legal entity can be matched across both. Check both sides use the identifier the same way; padding and blanks have faked matches before.

       count(*) as n_loan_level_mortgage_application_records

group by 1
order by 2 desc
limit 100;

entries.means: Splits registrations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means registration ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_registration as (
  select REGISTRATION_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_FEMA_IA_HOUSING_REGISTRATIONS
  where REGISTRATION_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_registration;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many commitment records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits commitment records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means commitment record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_commitment_record as (
  select COMMITMENT_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_FIRM_COMMITMENTS
  where COMMITMENT_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_commitment_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contract records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contract records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contract record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contract_record as (
  select CONTRACT_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_HUD_MF_SECTION8_CONTRACTS
  where CONTRACT_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contract_record;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.HOUSING.HOUSING__FED_USDA_RD_MFH_ACTIVE_PROJECTS
  where BORROWER_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many enrollments appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits enrollments into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means enrollment ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_enrollment as (
  select ENROLLMENT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_CMS_HOSPICE_ENROLLMENTS
  where ENROLLMENT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_enrollment;

entries.question: How many cases appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits cases into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means case number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_case as (
  select CASE_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_DOL_OFLC
  where CASE_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_case;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many public water systems appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits public water systems into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means PWSID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_public_water_system as (
  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_SERVICE_AREAS
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_public_water_system;

entries.question: How many public water systems have at least ten areas?

  select PWSID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_SERVICE_AREAS
  where PWSID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(*) as n_public_water_systems_with_10_or_more
from per_public_water_system
where n >= 10;

)

from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many stints appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits stints into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means stint ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_stint as (
  select STINT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.IMMIGRATION.IMMIGRATION__FED_ICE_DETENTION_STINTS
  where STINT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_stint;

entries.question: How many cases appear more than once (going by case ID)?
entries.means: Splits cases into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means case ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_case as (
  select CASE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUDICIARY.JUDICIARY__FED_OYEZ
  where CASE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_case;

select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.means: Splits courts into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means court ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_court as (
  select COURT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_COURTHOUSES
  where COURT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_court;

select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

entries.question: How many name suffixes appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits name suffixes into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means name suffix is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_name_suffix as (
  select NAME_SUFFIX, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_JUDGES
  where NAME_SUFFIX is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_name_suffix;

entries.question: How many opinion clusters appear more than once?

  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_COURTLISTENER_OPINION_CLUSTERS
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_opinion_cluster;

entries.question: How many companies appear more than once?

entries.sql:
with per_company as (
  select COMPANY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_FHFA_SUSPENDED_COUNTERPARTIES
  where COMPANY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_company;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many appeal records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits appeal records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means appeal record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_appeal_record as (
  select APPEAL_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_APPELLATE
  where APPEAL_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_appeal_record;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.question: How many defendant records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits defendant records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means defendant record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_defendant_record as (
  select DEFENDANT_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_FJC_IDB_CRIMINAL
  where DEFENDANT_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_defendant_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many votes appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits votes into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means vote ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_vote as (
  select VOTE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__FED_SCDB
  where VOTE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_vote;

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__INTL_EURLEX_CELLAR
  where CELEX_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_celex;

entries.question: How many entity logicals appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits entity logicals into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means entity logical ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_entity_logical as (
  select ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__INTL_EU_SANCTIONS
  where ENTITY_LOGICAL_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_entity_logical;

entries.question: How many records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_record as (
  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__INTL_UCDP_GED
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_record;
