entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many registrants appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits registrants into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means registrant name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_registrant as (
  select REGISTRANT_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__STATE_MO_SEX_OFFENDER_REGISTRY
  where REGISTRANT_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_registrant;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many references appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits references into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means reference number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_reference as (
  select REFERENCE_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__XC_UN_CONSOLIDATED_SANCTIONS_LIST
  where REFERENCE_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_reference;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many fatal encounters appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits fatal encounters into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_fatal_encounter as (
  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.JUSTICE.JUSTICE__XC_WAPO_FATAL_FORCE
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_fatal_encounter;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many documents appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits documents into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means document no is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_document as (
  select DOCUMENT_NO, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_MSHA_ACCIDENTS
  where DOCUMENT_NO is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_document;

entries.question: How many mines appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits mines into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means mine ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_mine as (
  select MINE_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_MSHA_MINES
  where MINE_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_mine;

entries.question: How many events appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits events into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means event no is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_event as (
  select EVENT_NO, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_MSHA_VIOLATIONS
  where EVENT_NO is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_event;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many individual workplace injuries appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits individual workplace injuries into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_individual_workplace_injury as (
  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_OSHA_ITA_CASE_DETAIL_2023
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_individual_workplace_injury;

entries.question: How many individual workplace injuries appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits individual workplace injuries into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_individual_workplace_injury as (
  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_OSHA_ITA_CASE_DETAIL_2024
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_individual_workplace_injury;

entries.question: How many individual workplace injuries appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits individual workplace injuries into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_individual_workplace_injury as (
  select ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_OSHA_ITA_CASE_DETAIL_2025
  where ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_individual_workplace_injury;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many cases appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits cases into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means case number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_case as (
  select CASE_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.LABOR.LABOR__FED_PBGC_TRUSTEED_PLANS
  where CASE_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_case;

entries.question: How many ships appear more than once (going by mmsi)?
entries.means: Splits ships into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means mmsi is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_ship as (
  select MMSI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.MARITIME.MARITIME__FED_NOAA_AIS
  where MMSI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_ship;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many bills appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits bills into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means bill number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_bill as (
  select BILL_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__BILLS
  where BILL_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_bill;

entries.question: How many filings appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits filings into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means filing ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_filing as (
  select FILING_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__CA_LOBBY_COVER
  where FILING_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_filing;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many lobbyists appear more than once (going by lobbyist ID)?
entries.means: Splits lobbyists into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means lobbyist ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_lobbyist as (
  select LOBBYIST_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__CA_LOBBY_FIRM_LOBBYIST
  where LOBBYIST_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_lobbyist;

entries.question: How many candidates show up for the first time each year?
entries.means: New arrivals - first year each candidate is seen. Swap min for max for last seen, the closest thing here to a death date.
entries.sql:
with first_seen as (
  select CAND_ID, min(year(ripple_ts)) as yr
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TIMELINE.POLITICS__FEC_CANDIDATE_SUMMARY
  where ripple_ts is not null and CAND_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select yr, count(*) as n_new
from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.question: How many candidates appear more than once?

with per_candidate as (
  select CAND_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__FEC_CANDIDATE_SUMMARY
  where CAND_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_candidate;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.question: How many candidates appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits candidates into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means candidate name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_candidate as (
  select CANDIDATE_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__FED_MEDSL_SENATE_RETURNS
  where CANDIDATE_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_candidate;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many judges appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits judges into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means judge name is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_judge as (
  select JUDGE_NAME, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__FJC_APPOINTMENT
  where JUDGE_NAME is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_judge;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many form IDs appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits form IDs into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means form ID number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_form_id as (
  select FORM_ID_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__IRS527_8871_ORGS
  where FORM_ID_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_form_id;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many members appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits members into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means member key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_member as (
  select MEMBER_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__MEMBER_CROSSWALK
  where MEMBER_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_member;

entries.means: Splits member of Congresses into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means bioguide is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_member_of_congress as (
  select BIOGUIDE, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__MEMBER_MONEY_RAISED
  where BIOGUIDE is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_member_of_congress;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contribution records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contribution records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contribution record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contribution_record as (
  select CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__ST_NYC_CFB_CAMPAIGN_2001_CONTRIBUTION
  where CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contribution_record;

entries.question: How many contribution records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contribution records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contribution record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contribution_record as (
  select CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__ST_NYC_CFB_CAMPAIGN_2009_CONTRIBUTION
  where CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contribution_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contribution records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contribution records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contribution record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contribution_record as (
  select CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__ST_NYC_CFB_CAMPAIGN_2013_CONTRIBUTION
  where CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contribution_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contribution records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contribution records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contribution record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contribution_record as (
  select CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__ST_NYC_CFB_CAMPAIGN_2021_CONTRIBUTIONS
  where CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contribution_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many contribution records appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contribution records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contribution record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contribution_record as (
  select CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__ST_NYC_CFB_CAMPAIGN_2025_CONTRIBUTIONS
  where CONTRIBUTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contribution_record;

entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__TX_LOBBY_AWARDS
  where REPORT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__TX_LOBBY_ENTERTAINMENT
  where REPORT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__TX_LOBBY_GIFTS

  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__TX_LOBBY_INDIVIDUAL_REPORTING
  where REPORT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many reports appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits reports into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means report ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_report as (
  select REPORT_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.POLITICS.POLITICS__TX_LOBBY_SUBJECT_MATTER
  where REPORT_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_report;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many federal award recipients appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits federal award recipients into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means UEI is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_federal_award_recipient as (
  select UEI, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.PROCUREMENT.PROCUREMENT__FED_SAM_EXCLUSIONS
  where UEI is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_federal_award_recipient;

entries.question: How many contract transactions appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits contract transactions into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means contract transaction unique key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_contract_transaction as (
  select CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.PROCUREMENT.PROCUREMENT__FED_USASPENDING_BULK
  where CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_contract_transaction;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one

entries.question: How many itis publications appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits itis publications into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means itis publications key is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_itis_publications as (
  select ITIS_PUBLICATIONS_KEY, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.REFERENCE.REFERENCE__FED_ITIS_PUBLICATIONS
  where ITIS_PUBLICATIONS_KEY is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_itis_publications;

       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,

entries.question: How many name citations appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits name citations into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means name citation ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_name_citation as (
  select NAME_CITATION_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.REFERENCE.REFERENCE__FED_USGS_GNIS_ALL_NAMES
  where NAME_CITATION_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_name_citation;

entries.question: How many leads appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits leads into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means lead ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_lead as (
  select LEAD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.REVIEW.LEAD_QUEUE
  where LEAD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_lead;

)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_award;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many appls appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits appls into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means appl ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_appl as (
  select APPL_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.SCIENCE_RESEARCH.SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_NIH_REPORTER
  where APPL_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_appl;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many scientific papers appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits scientific papers into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_scientific_paper as (
  select RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.SCIENCE_RESEARCH.SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_RETRACTION_WATCH
  where RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_scientific_paper;

entries.question: How many retraction pubmeds have at least ten scientific papers?
entries.means: The concentrated end - swap ten for your own line. Backs any claim that a few retraction pubmeds account for most scientific papers.
entries.sql:
with per_retraction_pubmed as (
  select RETRACTION_PUBMED_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.SCIENCE_RESEARCH.SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_RETRACTION_WATCH
  where RETRACTION_PUBMED_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(*) as n_retraction_pubmeds_with_10_or_more
from per_retraction_pubmed
where n >= 10;

  select AWARD_RECORD_ID, min(year(ripple_ts)) as yr
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TIMELINE.SCIENCE_RESEARCH__FED_SBIR_STTR_AWARDS
  where ripple_ts is not null and AWARD_RECORD_ID is not null

)

from first_seen
group by 1
order by 1;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many retraction records appear more than once (going by retraction record ID)?
entries.means: Splits retraction records into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means retraction record ID is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_retraction_record as (
  select RETRACTION_RECORD_ID, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.SCIENCE_RESEARCH.SCIENCE_RESEARCH__XC_RETRACTION_WATCH_DATABASE
  where RETRACTION_RECORD_ID is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_retraction_record;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many serials appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits serials into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means serial number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_serial as (
  select SERIAL_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_AIRCRAFT_REGISTRY
  where SERIAL_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_serial;

entries.question: How many serials appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits serials into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means serial number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_serial as (
  select SERIAL_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_FAA_REGISTRY
  where SERIAL_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_serial;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many incidents appear more than once (going by incident number)?
entries.means: Splits incidents into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means incident number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_incident as (
  select INCIDENT_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CASUALTIES
  where INCIDENT_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_incident;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many incidents appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits incidents into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means incident number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_incident as (
  select INCIDENT_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_CROSSING_INCIDENTS
  where INCIDENT_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_incident;

entries.kind: How many show up more than once
entries.question: How many accidents appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits accidents into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means accident number is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_accident as (
  select ACCIDENT_NUMBER, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_FRA_EQUIPMENT_ACCIDENTS
  where ACCIDENT_NUMBER is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_accident;

entries.question: How many ntsbs appear more than once?
entries.means: Splits ntsbs into once vs. repeats. Almost none repeating means ntsb no is a real one-per-row key; almost all repeating means it's a grouping column, and any 'top ten' is really who appears most.
entries.sql:
with per_ntsb as (
  select NTSB_NO, count(*) as n
  from LIBRARY_MARTS.TRANSPORT.TRANSPORT__FED_NTSB_AVIATION_EVENTS
  where NTSB_NO is not null
  group by 1
)
select count(case when n = 1 then 1 end) as appears_once,
       count(case when n > 1 then 1 end) as appears_more_than_once,
       max(n)                            as most_for_one
from per_ntsb;
